## Security Concerns
<!-- Found during setup. Never include secret values. -->

- `src/main/binaries.ts`, `get()`: tool downloads have no fetch timeout and no retry, so a stalled connection can
  leave the setup screen waiting indefinitely. (Availability, not integrity: checksums still gate every install.)
- Not defended by design (stated in `README.md`): same-user programs can read `pairing.json` and the extension's
  storage; any local process can fill the server's 16 connections or hold its port.

## Inconsistencies
<!-- Pattern / naming / config deviations. -->

- `src/main/server/pairing.ts`: its refusal texts carry no error code; `ipc.ts` maps the two known ones by value
  (`pairingRefusal`) and passes any other text on in English. Confirm no other refusal can reach the window.
- `src/shared/protocol.ts`: error tokens `busy`, `not_ready`, `unknown_request`, `storage_unavailable` and
  `bad_site` are declared but not produced on `main` (planned Phase 2 routes).

## Unverified Controls
<!-- Controls generated but not proven at runtime (see the capability report). -->

- `.claude/settings.json` deny rules and the raw-Git hook: generated and statically validated. Native Windows has
  no Claude OS sandbox, so a Node subprocess can still read denied files; the denies stop Claude's file tools and
  shell commands that name the file.
- Codex: the deny-read permission profile is a user-level snippet that project-setup does not install. Until it
  is added to the user config and checked with a canary run, Codex lanes are protected by instruction only.
- The reviewer is read-only by instruction in Codex (no `default_permissions` profile in
  `.codex/agents/reviewer.toml`).
